summary_ja: 事業法人等向けエクスポージャーのマチュリティ(実効マチュリティの算式、一年の下限・五年の上限、短期取引の例外、ネッティング契約の場合の取扱い)を定める。
summary_en: Defines the effective maturity formula for corporate, etc. exposures with its one-year floor and five-year cap, exceptions for short-term exposures, and treatment of netting contracts and the expected exposure method.
paragraphs: The maturity used in the formula for the amount of credit risk-weighted assets of corporate, etc. exposures shall be the effective maturity calculated by the following formula; provided, however, that where it is less than one year it shall be one year, and where it exceeds five years it shall be five years. {{F:p174i0}} CF_{t} is the cash flow that the obligor may contractually pay to the creditor in period t.

Where an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach is unable to calculate the effective maturity of contractual payment obligations, it may, in place of the formula in the preceding paragraph, use the contractual remaining term of the exposure or another conservative value.

Notwithstanding the proviso to paragraph (1), the lower limit of one year shall not apply to short-term exposures falling under the following items whose original contractual maturity is less than one year. In this case, an effective maturity of one day or more shall be used as the maturity. (i) Exposures arising from repo-style transactions (limited to those satisfying the contractual forms generally used for transactions of the same kind), call transactions and other short-term money market transactions. (ii) Exposures arising from other capital market transactions satisfying all of the following requirements: (a) Sufficient protection by collateral is continuously maintained. (b) It is contractually provided that the transaction is marked to market every business day and is subject to margining. (c) It is contractually provided that, upon the counterparty's loss of the benefit of time or failure to perform obligations relating to margining, the collateral can be promptly disposed of or set off. (iii) Short-term and highly liquid trade transactions, trade-related letter of credit transactions and the like. (iv) Short-term and highly liquid trade-related contingent liabilities and the like not included in the preceding item. (v) Exposures arising from transactions for settling securities, etc. or funds (excluding derivative transactions).

Notwithstanding the preceding three paragraphs, the effective maturity of revolving exposures shall be the period until the date on which the contract for the transaction terminates, or another conservative value.

For derivative transactions or transactions provided in paragraph (3) that are subject to a legally effective bilateral netting contract, the maturity weighted by notional principal amount or other nominal amount of those transactions shall be used in calculating the effective maturity provided in paragraph (1).

Notwithstanding the preceding paragraph, the maturity of transactions falling under paragraph (3) that are subject to a legally effective bilateral netting contract shall have as its lower limit the minimum holding period provided in Article 76, paragraph (2), item (i) (where the transactions covered by that bilateral netting contract include individual transactions falling under (a) through (c) of that item that fall under multiple minimum holding periods, the longest of the minimum holding periods of those individual transactions); provided, however, that where that item makes no provision, the lower limit shall be five days.

Where an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach applies Articles 49 through 54 mutatis mutandis to the EAD of corporate, etc. exposures under paragraph (5) of the preceding Article, the maturity used in the formula for the amount of credit risk-weighted assets of corporate, etc. exposures shall be the effective maturity calculated by the formula in item (i), and the effective EE_{tk} in that item shall be the amount calculated by the formula in item (ii); provided, however, that where the effective maturity is less than one year it shall be one year, and where it exceeds five years it shall be five years. (i) {{F:p175i0}} Δt_{k} is t_{k} − t_{k−1}. df_{k} is the discount factor at the risk-free rate over the future period t_{k}. EE_{tk} is the expected exposure at future time t_{k} (EE_{t0} is the current exposure). m is the index m of t_{m}, where t_{m} is the last of the future times t_{k} at which the exposure amount is measured that does not exceed one year. n is the index n of t_{n}, where t_{n} is the last of the future times t_{k} at which the exposure amount is measured that does not exceed the time of maturity. (ii) Effective EE_{tk} = max(effective EE_{tk−1}, EE_{tk}). Effective EE_{t0} is the current exposure.

Notwithstanding the preceding paragraph, where the longest maturity among all transactions constituting a netting set is less than one year and all transactions are transactions relating to those listed in the items of paragraph (3), that netting set shall be regarded as a single exposure and paragraphs (1) through (6) shall apply.
